pointers.sentence: Importing `django` does almost nothing: the package's own module defines a version and one function (`django/__init__.py`).
`django.conf.settings` is a `LazySettings`: a stand-in for the project's settings (`django/conf/__init__.py:settings`).
`django.apps.apps` is an `Apps`, the **app registry**: the record of the installed applications and of the model classes (`django/apps/registry.py:apps`).

Startup never says "load the settings": whichever line of code first reads or writes a setting does it (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings._setup`, `django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject.__setattr__`).

It stays empty until `Apps.populate` is called with the list of applications, and until then, where settings can be read, it refuses most questions with `AppRegistryNotReady` (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.populate`, `django/apps/registry.py:Apps.check_apps_ready`).

`django.setup` is the function that takes a process from the one state to the other, from having imported Django to being able to use it (`django/__init__.py:setup`).

The script prefix is the part of a URL's path that belongs to the server's mount point, which the URLs Django generates have to begin with (`django/urls/base.py:set_script_prefix`, `django/urls/base.py:reverse`).

The script prefix is the part of a URL's path that belongs to the server's mount point, which the URLs Django generates have to begin with (`django/urls/base.py:set_script_prefix`, `django/urls/base.py:reverse`).

Under a server it is set for each request served, ordinarily to `FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME` or else to what the server says the site is mounted under ([The script prefix, the current URLconf and the caches](urls/state.md#the-script-prefix)) (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.handle`).

Under a server it is set for each request served, ordinarily to `FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME` or else to what the server says the site is mounted under ([The script prefix, the current URLconf and the caches](urls/state.md#the-script-prefix)) (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.handle`).

Nothing imported during the first phase can define a model, not even a model of an application whose configuration is already made, because a model's class statement asks the registry which application it belongs to, and the registry will not say until every entry has its configuration (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.get_containing_app_config`).

A models module cannot fetch another application's model with `Apps.get_model` while the second phase runs, unless it passes `require_ready=False`, and then `get_model` imports that application's models module itself if its turn has not yet come (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.get_model`).
From then on a script that relied on `"DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE"` had to call `django.setup` itself, or meet `AppRegistryNotReady` (`docs/releases/1.7.txt`).

Under a server it is `get_wsgi_application` or `get_asgi_application`, which the project's `wsgi.py` or `asgi.py` calls as the server imports it; each calls `django.setup` and then makes the handler, the object the server will call with every request (`django/core/wsgi.py:get_wsgi_application`, `django/core/asgi.py:get_asgi_application`).

Under a server it is `get_wsgi_application` or `get_asgi_application`, which the project's `wsgi.py` or `asgi.py` calls as the server imports it; each calls `django.setup` and then makes the handler, the object the server will call with every request (`django/core/wsgi.py:get_wsgi_application`, `django/core/asgi.py:get_asgi_application`).
For a management command it is ordinarily `ManagementUtility.execute`, before it looks for the command (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.execute`).

A call after one that succeeded finds the registry ready, and `Apps.populate` returns at once; but logging is ordinarily configured again, which under a project's `LOGGING` can disable loggers made between the two calls (`django/utils/log.py:configure_logging`; [Logging](startup/logging.md)).
`SecurityMiddleware` reads its settings into attributes once, in its constructor, when the middleware chain is made (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.__init__`).

The template engines are made at their first use, from `settings.TEMPLATES` as it then stood, and kept (`django/template/utils.py:EngineHandler.templates`, `django/template/utils.py:EngineHandler.__getitem__`).

A model's `_meta` caches lists of fields that depend on which other models exist (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.related_objects`).
So a setting assigned in a running process changes what the next read of it returns, and nothing that was built from the old value (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__setattr__`).
